summary: Iteration 7 — Weekly Menu Management feature verified end-to-end. Backend: 13/13 pytest tests pass covering GET/PUT/DELETE /api/admin/weekly-menu (14 slots, upsert, whitespace trim, invalid-day validation, delete + repeat-delete-404, non-admin 403), GET /api/weekly-menu (14 slots, auth-required 401), GET /api/weekly-menu/today (resolves items with today's weekday), menu resolution precedence (weekly template applied when no override, date-specific override wins, fallback returns after override delete), and regression on date-specific menu CRUD. Frontend: All UI flows verified — admin Menu tab renders new 'Weekly menu' card with 7 day cards × 2 meal slots (breakfast/dinner) each with textarea + Save + trash; saving updates the '{n} items' badge and shows 'Weekly menu updated' toast; reload preserves saved items; window.confirm dialog on clear works and badge reverts to 'empty'; chef dashboard resolves today's weekly items in data-testid='chef-breakfast-menu' and data-testid='chef-dinner-menu' cards while total counters still render; employee dashboard shows 'On the menu' block with weekly-template items via data-testid='menu-dinner'. No new bugs found.
action_items: None blocking. Feature works as specified.
critical_code_review_comments: AdminDashboard.jsx has grown to 1125 lines (previous review already flagged this). The new Weekly Menu section (~85 lines in a single JSX block) further compounds the maintenance risk. Recommend extracting a WeeklyMenuCard.jsx component (state + JSX for a single day) and a WeeklyMenuSection.jsx wrapper.

server.py _resolve_menu_for (line 709): the date-specific override 'wins' only when items list is non-empty (`if doc and doc.get('items')`). An admin who intentionally sets a date-specific override with an empty list will silently fall back to the weekly template — which may be surprising. Consider treating any existing override doc as authoritative, or documenting the coexist rule clearly.
PUT /api/admin/weekly-menu accepts an unlimited number of items; consider capping items length and per-item length (like other endpoints) to prevent unbounded documents.
GET /api/weekly-menu/today uses server-local 'today'. If frontend and server are in different TZs, chef/employee could see the wrong weekday. Consider passing client date or documenting this.

success_rate.frontend: 100% (admin weekly save/clear/persist, chef today menu, employee menu display all verified)
